subject: shotgun
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: shotgun, in the place of the game's models/v_shotgun.mdl, models/p_shotgun.mdl, models/w_shotgun.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_crowbar.mdl, models/w_9mmar.mdl, models/w_357.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked B, D, B, A where the asset was C, B, A, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The outline is a long gun of about the right length, but its stock end curls into a hook. The FRONT-LEFT, BACK-RIGHT, TOP and BELOW views each show the rear bending about 90 degrees down. A pump-action combat shotgun has a straight or slightly angled stock, so the silhouette is not the brief's shape. The bend is in the outline itself, not only in the paint.

M2.reason: Measured length 28.2 against the 30 asked, 6% off, within 15%. Width 17.1 and height 3.8 are the measured extents and give no conflict with the brief.

M3.reason: Present: a barrel with a small front-sight tab (top and front views), a ribbed forend on the middle section (RIGHT, LEFT and attack frames), a receiver and a rear end. Missing or unreadable: the pistol grip and trigger guard do not show in any side view, and the rear is a hook where a shotgun has a butt stock. A part the brief asks for is absent or in the wrong form, so this stays at 1.

M4.reason: Dark gunmetal throughout, with the pump and stock in the same dark tone, as the brief asks for black metal with a dark pump and stock. Highlights on the receiver and forend read as metal, not as a different colour.

M5.reason: The side views (LEFT, RIGHT, FRONT-RIGHT) show mottled, dithered green-grey blotches along the barrel and stock. They read as camouflage or noise rather than a clean black metal finish, a paint fault in the picture, not a shape fault.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the rubric for this leg. The line-up test measured the asset passing: in the four readings the judges never picked it as the one not made by Valve. In lineup.png it sits as A beside Valve's 9mm SMG, .357 and crowbar and reads as one of the game's guns.

M7.reason: The barrel end is forward, with the front sight at the front and the rear at the back, and the model stands upright as held in first-person.png and in-hand.png, barrel up. Nothing in the views shows it lying or rolled.

M8.reason: SMAK check reports no errors. 174 triangles is under the third quartile (187) of Half-Life's props of its kind, so no triangle fault. The views show a solid body: the muzzle opening is the only open end, and it is the barrel's normal front. No floating or inverted parts seen.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the weapon sits in the same place and the same way round as the game's own (both at the same spot over the orange hand, barrel up-left). In attack.png the gun stays over the hand in every frame from SHOOT 0/20 to 20/20, and the hand is still under it.
